editorial.headline: Rail Signalling and Telecoms Installation: Open Nationally, Viable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the systems that help railway signalling and communications work, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
This activity is the practical work of installing, maintaining and repairing railway signalling and telecommunications systems. It includes, for example, electrical signals running alongside the track. The scope is therefore not simply about supplying equipment: it is about putting these systems in place and keeping them operational through maintenance and repair.

It suits enterprises whose work sits directly within that installation-and-upkeep chain. The record makes it available across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the classification is not reserved for one particular business scale. What matters is that the registered activity remains within railway signalling and telecommunications installation, maintenance or repair.

Nationally, the PMA position is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level for this activity. That openness is grounded in the cited presidential regulations; it is not a conclusion drawn from a neighbouring business category or from a general assumption about rail infrastructure.

Bali does not overturn that national position. The province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for low and medium-low risk activities, but this activity is not blocked by that rule. At the Besar scale, the record identifies its OSS risk as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—medium-high/high—which is why the moratorium does not apply. Bali’s recorded status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: a foreign-owned registration is not barred there by the stated moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not overturn the national position: this activity is not blocked by the stated moratorium.
